The words replaced are his, so the card shows them first. DOES WHAT THE_CHANGE SAYS: Emulate's sentence replaces his one, and his 'genuinely' is back ('two genuinely safe things to do'). The draft appears once in the context, exactly as in DRAFT. The contrast with the manipulative sentence above ('whatever you answer, you end up doing what the speaker wants') is as sharp as in his pair: no way out versus two safe ways. 'Routes' to 'things to do' loses the path image but none of the claim, and the example right after it (allow warmth, or allow space) is two things to do. 'someone' is just the person asked, not a new party. No new fact, claim, first-person detail, study or name. It is wordier and plainer than his crisp 'An ethical one offers two genuinely safe routes', but it is not a tidy summary and carries no hedge. The weakest point: his 'An ethical one' becomes the full name, so 'Ethical Double Bind Question(s)' now appears in two sentences in a row (the next, unchanged, is 'Ethical Double Bind Questions might be:'), on top of 'Manipulative Double Bind Questions' in the sentence before. T19 and T25 sit in the unchanged 'might be:' line, not in the draft. T17 and T20: it is a definition, mid-section, not an aphorism or a closer. C02: the draft has no pronoun to mislead.
